questions.question: What is the inferred type of let count = 3; when no type annotation is supplied?
questions.explanation: A mutable let binding initialized with a number literal usually widens to number.

questions.question: A value has type string | number. Which check narrows it to string in the true branch?
questions.explanation: TypeScript recognizes typeof checks as type guards and narrows the true branch to string.

questions.question: Which type accepts arbitrary input while requiring a type check or assertion before accessing its properties?
questions.explanation: unknown can hold arbitrary values, but property access requires the compiler to know more about the value.

questions.question: Which type describes a two-element array whose first element is a string and whose second is a number?
questions.explanation: A tuple describes the types at specific positions.

questions.question: What does the type User = { name: string; age?: number } allow? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: name is required and must be a string. age may be omitted or supplied as a number.

questions.question: Which declaration preserves the input type as the return type for identity calls with different kinds of values?

options.d: function identity(x: string | number): string | number

questions.explanation: The generic type parameter T ties the return type to the argument type for each call.

questions.question: What is keyof { id: number; title: string }?
questions.explanation: keyof gives the union of a type's property keys.

questions.question: Which utility type keeps only id and name from User?
questions.explanation: Pick selects the specified keys from the original object type.

questions.question: Which type makes the top-level properties of User optional for a patch payload?
questions.explanation: Partial makes each top-level property optional while retaining its value type.

questions.question: Which statements about TypeScript's compile-time types are true? Select all that apply.

options.a: An interface validates API responses at runtime
options.b: A type assertion can change the compiler's view of an expression
options.c: Casting with as number converts a string to a number at runtime
options.d: An interface declaration does not create a runtime constructor

questions.explanation: Assertions and interfaces inform type checking. They do not perform runtime conversion or validation.

questions.question: A union has variants { kind: 'success'; data: string } and { kind: 'failure'; error: Error }. What check lets the compiler permit result.data?
questions.explanation: The literal kind property discriminates the union, so the true branch has the success variant.

questions.question: With strictNullChecks enabled, what happens when const title: string = null; is checked?

options.a: null is converted to an empty string
options.b: The checker reports a type error
options.c: The type widens to string | null
options.d: The checker reports no error because null matches string

questions.explanation: With strict null checking, null must be explicitly included in the type for this assignment to be valid.

questions.question: A function accepts { name: string }. Can it accept a variable declared as const employee = { name: 'Ada', id: 1 };?

options.a: Yes, the variable has the required name property with the right type
options.b: No, the two object types must have exactly the same keys
options.c: No, only instances of a named class can be passed
options.d: Yes, but only after deleting employee.id

questions.explanation: Structural assignability checks that the variable supplies the required members. Its additional id does not prevent assignment.

questions.question: Which type represents a branch that is impossible after all variants of a union have been handled?
questions.explanation: never represents an impossible value and can be used to check that a union switch is exhaustive.

questions.question: Given const tags: readonly string[] = ['new'];, which operations are allowed by the type checker? Select all that apply.

options.d: Make a mutable copy with const copy = [...tags];

questions.explanation: A readonly array permits reads and copying. Its type disallows mutating methods and index assignments.

questions.question: For a plain object literal, which syntax infers readonly properties with literal value types?
questions.explanation: A const assertion prevents literal widening and marks the literal object's properties readonly in the type system.

questions.question: What is the purpose of const palette = expression satisfies Palette;?

options.b: Change each property to the any type
options.c: Emit a Palette instance instead of the expression
options.d: Check compatibility with Palette without replacing the expression's inferred type with Palette

questions.explanation: satisfies checks assignability while retaining the type inferred for the expression.

questions.question: Which return annotation makes isUser(value) a type guard that can narrow value in an if block?
questions.explanation: The value is User annotation is a type predicate tied to the function parameter.

questions.question: Which type requires a number value for each key in the union 'read' | 'write'?
questions.explanation: Record maps each key in the first type argument to the value type in the second.

questions.question: Which checks can narrow value from string | number | null to a single primitive type in their true branches? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: The typeof checks each select one union member. Excluding null still leaves string and number.
